name: btree_merge128
prose: Inline wrapper that calls btree_merge(&target->h, &victim->h, &btree_geo128, gfp) and returns its result. btree_merge BUG()s if target == victim. If target is empty (target->node is NULL) it takes over victim's root node and height and re-initialises victim to empty, returning 0 without allocating. Otherwise it repeatedly takes victim's last entry, inserts it into target with gfp, and removes it from victim, so entries are moved, not copied; it returns 0 once victim is empty. If an insertion fails it returns that error (btree_insert returns -ENOMEM) immediately: entries already moved are in target, the entry that failed and all remaining entries are still in victim.
note: btree_merge in lib/btree.c:634 moves entries (btree_remove(victim, ...) after each btree_insert) and has BUG_ON(target == victim); reviewer rounds 1 and 15 were right about the BUG_ON precondition and about victim being modified; the round 2 claim that victim keeps all entries on failure is wrong (moved entries are removed from victim).

name: static inline int BTREE_FN(init)(BTREE_TYPE_HEAD *head)
prose: Generated typed wrapper (the function btree_init<suffix> once BTREE_FN and BTREE_TYPE_HEAD are expanded) that returns btree_init(&head->h). btree_init (lib/btree.c:188) initialises the head as empty, then creates the node mempool with mempool_create(0, btree_alloc, btree_free, NULL); it returns -ENOMEM if mempool_create returns NULL and 0 otherwise. The wrapper itself only forwards that result.
note: Reviewer (round 15) said there is no -ENOMEM path: wrong, lib/btree.c:188-195 returns -ENOMEM when mempool_create fails. The old prose said 'initial node allocation', which was imprecise (it is the mempool creation); corrected.

name: __can_cc_frame_bits
prose: Function-like macro, an expression with no side effects of its own (it evaluates its arguments, some more than once). Let n = (is_eff ? CAN_FRAME_HEADER_EFF_BITS (39) : CAN_FRAME_HEADER_SFF_BITS (19)) + data_len * BITS_PER_BYTE + CAN_FRAME_CRC_FIELD_BITS (16). If bitstuffing is nonzero the stuffed part is n + (n - 1) / 4 (integer division), otherwise n. The macro yields that stuffed part plus CAN_FRAME_FOOTER_BITS (9), plus CAN_INTERMISSION_BITS (3) if intermission is nonzero. No range check is done on data_len.
note: Macro, not a function: kept as a described macro; the earlier contract used an unbound logic function so none is given.

name: __can_fd_frame_bits
prose: Function-like macro, an expression with no side effects of its own (it evaluates its arguments, some more than once). Let n = (is_eff ? CANFD_FRAME_HEADER_EFF_BITS (41) : CANFD_FRAME_HEADER_SFF_BITS (22)) + data_len * BITS_PER_BYTE. If bitstuffing is nonzero the stuffed part is n + (n - 1) / 4 (integer division), otherwise n. The macro yields that stuffed part plus a CRC field of CANFD_FRAME_CRC17_FIELD_BITS (28) when data_len <= 16 or CANFD_FRAME_CRC21_FIELD_BITS (33) otherwise (the CRC field is not itself stuffed), plus CAN_FRAME_FOOTER_BITS (9), plus CAN_INTERMISSION_BITS (3) if intermission is nonzero. No range check is done on data_len.
note: Macro, not a function: kept as a described macro; no contract (unbound logic function in the earlier attempt).

name: can_frame_bits
prose: Function-like macro: if is_fd is nonzero it evaluates to __can_fd_frame_bits(is_eff, bitstuffing, intermission, data_len), otherwise to __can_cc_frame_bits(is_eff, bitstuffing, intermission, data_len). Only one branch of the conditional is evaluated. Its doc comment describes the result as the number of bits on the wire of a CAN frame; no sanitising of data_len is done.
note: Macro that selects between two other macros; described rather than dropped because the selection is its whole behaviour.

name: can_frame_bytes
prose: Function-like macro that evaluates to DIV_ROUND_UP(can_frame_bits(is_fd, is_eff, bitstuffing, true, data_len), BITS_PER_BYTE): the frame bit count with the intermission always included (intermission is passed as true), rounded up to a whole number of bytes. data_len is not range checked.
note: Macro; no contract (unbound logic function in the earlier attempt).

name: CIRC_CNT
prose: Function-like macro: expands to ((head) - (tail)) & ((size) - 1), the number of occupied slots of a circular buffer. It gives the intended count only if size is a power of two; with that, the result is (head - tail) modulo size. It does not check that head and tail are in range.
note: Macro; contract dropped (bit operations on a bool-typed result tripped Frama-C earlier, and a macro has no parameters types).

name: CIRC_SPACE
prose: Function-like macro: expands to CIRC_CNT(tail, head + 1, size), i.e. ((tail) - ((head) + 1)) & ((size) - 1), the number of free slots. With a power-of-two size this is (tail - head - 1) modulo size, in the range 0 to size - 1: one slot is always kept unused so that a full buffer is distinguishable from an empty one. It does not check that head and tail are in range.
note: Macro; no contract.

name: CIRC_CNT_TO_END
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression that declares locals end = size - tail and n = ((head) + end) & (size - 1) and yields n < end ? n : end. With a power-of-two size, n is the occupied count (head - tail) modulo size, so the result is the smaller of the occupied count and size - tail: the number of occupied slots that can be read contiguously from tail without wrapping. Arguments head and tail are each read once.
note: Macro; no contract (CIRC_CNT unbound in the earlier attempt).

name: CIRC_SPACE_TO_END
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression that declares locals end = size - 1 - head and n = (end + tail) & (size - 1) and yields n <= end ? n : end + 1. With a power-of-two size, n is the free space (tail - head - 1) modulo size; the result is n when n <= size - 1 - head, otherwise size - head. That is the number of free slots that can be written contiguously from head without wrapping. Arguments head and tail are each read once.
note: Macro; no contract. Checked by example: size 8, head 5, tail 2 gives 3; size 8, head 5, tail 0 gives 2.

name: static inline void class_##_name##_destructor(_type *p)
prose: Generated by DEFINE_CLASS(_name, _type, _exit, _init, ...): copies *p into a local variable _T of type _type and then evaluates the _exit expression, which may use _T; it returns nothing. Whatever release happens is whatever _exit does; the function itself performs no other action. It is the cleanup function attached to variables declared with CLASS()/guard() via __cleanup, so it runs when such a variable leaves scope. EXTEND_CLASS and __DEFINE_UNLOCK_GUARD generate other functions of the same name pattern.
note: Old prose said the release happens 'exactly once' and that the instance came from the matching constructor; neither is checkable from the macro. Named by the definition head in DEFINE_CLASS.

name: static inline _type class_##_name##_constructor(_init_args)
prose: Generated by DEFINE_CLASS(_name, _type, _exit, _init, _init_args...): declares a local _type t initialised from the _init expression, using the _init_args parameters, and returns t. It reports no error by itself; for guards generated by DEFINE_GUARD the _init expression is ({ _lock; _T; }), so it runs the lock statement and returns the passed value, and DEFINE_GUARD_COND_4 variants may return ERR_PTR(_RET) as the value when the condition fails. __DEFINE_LOCK_GUARD_1 and __DEFINE_LOCK_GUARD_0 generate differently shaped constructors.
note: Named by the definition head in DEFINE_CLASS. Old claim of error handle on failure holds only for conditional guard variants.

name: static inline void *class_##_name##_lock_ptr(class_##_name##_t *_T)
prose: Generated by __DEFINE_GUARD_LOCK_PTR(_name, _exp): reads the pointer stored at *(_exp) into _ptr; if IS_ERR(_ptr) it returns NULL, otherwise it returns _ptr unchanged. So the result is NULL both for an error-encoded pointer and for a stored NULL, and non-NULL only for a stored non-error pointer. It changes no state. DEFINE_CLASS_IS_UNCONDITIONAL generates a variant of the same name that simply returns (void *)1, and DEFINE_GUARD_COND_4 generates an _ext variant that forwards to the base one.
note: Old prose said 'NULL iff the guard holds an error', which is wrong: a stored NULL also gives NULL. Named by the head in __DEFINE_GUARD_LOCK_PTR.

name: static inline int class_##_name##_lock_err(class_##_name##_t *_T)
prose: Generated by __DEFINE_GUARD_LOCK_PTR(_name, _exp): converts the stored value *(_exp) to a long _rc. If _rc is 0 it is replaced by -EBUSY; then, if _rc is not an error value (IS_ERR_VALUE false) it is replaced by 0. It returns 0 when the stored value is a non-error value other than 0, -EBUSY when the stored value is 0, and the stored negative errno itself when the stored value is in the error range. It changes no state. DEFINE_GUARD_COND_4 generates an _ext variant that forwards to the base one.
note: Old prose was right on 0 and -EBUSY but missed that the stored errno is returned as is. Named by the head in __DEFINE_GUARD_LOCK_PTR.

name: cnt32_to_63
prose: Function-like macro (a GNU statement expression) that keeps a function-local static u32 __m_cnt_hi at each expansion site. It reads that value as the high word, issues smp_rmb(), then evaluates cnt_lo once as the low word. If the top bits of the high and low words differ ((s32)(hi ^ lo) < 0) it stores (hi ^ 0x80000000) + (hi >> 31) into both the static and the local high word. Its value is the 64-bit combination of the high and low words, so the low 32 bits equal cnt_lo, and bit 63 is documented as garbage. The header comment states the conditions for the extension to work (called at least once per half period of the counter, not preempted for too long, cnt_lo read directly from the counter); the macro does not enforce them. It uses no lock; concurrent updaters may store the same value.
note: Prose-style contract dropped (it named identifiers not in the file and called the result monotonic unconditionally).

name: comedi_check_trigger_is_unique

name: fsleep
prose: Sleeps using one of three mechanisms chosen by usecs. If usecs <= 10 it calls udelay(usecs) (busy wait). Else if usecs < USLEEP_RANGE_UPPER_BOUND, which is (TICK_NSEC << 2) / NSEC_PER_USEC, it calls usleep_range(usecs, usecs + (usecs >> 2)), which sleeps in TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE. Otherwise it calls msleep(DIV_ROUND_UP(usecs, USEC_PER_MSEC)); msleep takes an unsigned int, so on a 64-bit unsigned long a rounded-up millisecond count above UINT_MAX is truncated by the call. It returns nothing and may sleep except in the udelay branch.
note: Reviewer right: the old prose said at least usecs microseconds with only an overflow precondition on usecs + (usecs >> 2); the msleep argument truncation is not excluded. Rewritten without a duration guarantee.

name: bool folio_test_hugetlb_##flname(struct folio *folio)
prose: Generated by TESTHPAGEFLAG via HPAGEFLAG(Temporary, temporary); the instance is folio_test_hugetlb_temporary(folio). When CONFIG_HUGETLB_PAGE is defined (the __always_inline version) it takes the address of folio->private and returns test_bit(HPG_temporary, private), i.e. whether bit 2 (HPG_temporary) of that word is set; it modifies nothing. When CONFIG_HUGETLB_PAGE is not defined the generated version ignores folio and returns 0. The function takes no lock; the header comment says that examinations of HPG_temporary other than right after allocation by code that knows it has the only reference require hugetlb_lock, which callers must follow.
note: Reviewer right: the old prose allowed lockless examination 'right after allocation'; the header comment only allows that for setting the flag, all other examinations and modifications need hugetlb_lock. Reworded to leave locking to the callers.

When CONFIG_HUGETLB_PAGE is defined (the __always_inline version) it takes the address of folio->private and calls set_bit(HPG_temporary, private), an atomic set of bit 2 of that word; it returns nothing. When CONFIG_HUGETLB_PAGE is not defined the generated version ignores folio and does nothing. The function takes no lock; the header comment says the flag may be set without hugetlb_lock when the code knows it has the only reference to a page just allocated from the buddy allocator.
note: Reviewer right on the locking comment (wording of the old prose mixed set and test). HPG_temporary is the third enumerator (0 restore_reserve, 1 migratable, 2 temporary).

The function takes no lock; the header comment says that modifications of this flag other than the initial set require hugetlb_lock, which callers must follow.
